rows.responsibility: Top-level media-view product lifecycle and state machine: typed open context, gallery/shared-media navigation, loading/streaming, playback controls, seek/speed/quality/fullscreen/PiP, call-aware pause/resume, system media controls, TTL/single-view burn, screenshot protection, save/share/delete/recognition, keyboard/touch/gesture input, hide/teardown and resource continuity; protected-message document bubbles must not auto-persist forbidsSaving media to disk/cache-file from updateControls
rows.state_machine: typed OpenRequest/context -> resolve/display static or streamed media -> controls/input/navigation/streaming updates -> optional fullscreen/PiP/quality transitions -> error/retry or close/hide -> persist eligible playback/window state -> burn/cleanup protected ephemeral state -> deterministic teardown
rows.side_effects: Persists media-view window/PiP geometry, playback speed/quality/last position where allowed; coordinates media loading and power-save blocker; drives screenshot protection and TTL read/burn; pauses/resumes around calls; exposes save/share/delete/recognition; owns keyboard/touch/gesture arbitration and clears transient timers/selections/stream state on hide. New b0d1fe5e delta removes the updateControls automatic DocumentSaveClickHandler::Save(ToCacheOrFile) path for forbidsSaving messages; protected media viewing must not create a disk persistence side effect merely to populate viewer controls.
rows.failure_cases: stale media or async recognition survives source/session replacement; playback position/quality lost or resurrected incorrectly; call pause resumes when it should not; failed stream loops without fail-closed fallback; PiP/fullscreen transition duplicates player ownership; TTL media survives close; screenshot protection drops on native handle changes; hidden viewer retains timers/stream/resources; viewer shortcuts steal control input. A forbidsSaving document being auto-written to disk/cache-file during viewer control refresh is a privacy/security failure.
rows.ui_disposition: Decompose into existing canonical MediaViewer/ConversationWorkspace, Chromium media element/compositor, canonical permissions/resource owners and platform adapters. Do not introduce Telegram OverlayWidget or a second media runtime. Canonical controls/components and source-neutral names only.
rows.fabushi_target: MAPPED OPEN. Implemented in canonical MediaViewer: Chromium native controls, replacement/unmount playback fencing, media-input arbitration, fullscreen Escape behavior, source-neutral volume/mute persistence and hashed per-source resumable playback position. Still open: call interruption, speed/quality policy, Media Session, deterministic PiP geometry/ownership, TTL/single-view, screenshot protection, recognition and broader service/platform composition. Rebaseline requirement: prove canonical MediaViewer never auto-persists protected/forbids-saving media as a side effect of rendering or control refresh.
rows.platform_differences: Qt window/RHI/event-filter mechanics are not copied. Electron/Chromium supplies media rendering/fullscreen/PiP primitives; Fabushi must preserve product lifecycle, durable state, security, input, error and accessibility semantics through its existing source-neutral owners.
